generalDesc: Supported file formats are DOCX, XLSX, XLS (Excel97~2003), PPT, PDF, TXT, JPEG, JPG, PNG, GIF, CSV, JSON, EML, HTML.
This method chunks files using a 'naive' method:
Use vision detection model to split the texts into smaller segments.
Then, combine adjacent segments until the token count exceeds the threshold specified by 'Chunk token number for text', at which point a chunk is created.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
qaDesc: This chunk method supports XLSX and CSV/TXT file formats.

If a file is in XLSX or XLS (Excel97~2003) format, it should contain two columns without headers: one for questions and the other for answers, with the question column preceding the answer column. Multiple sheets are acceptable, provided the columns are properly structured.
If a file is in CSV/TXT format, it must be UTF-8 encoded with TAB as the delimiter to separate questions and answers.
Lines of texts that fail to follow the above rules will be ignored, and each Q&A pair will be considered a distinct chunk.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
resumeDesc: Supported file formats are DOCX, PDF, TXT.
Résumés of various forms are parsed and organized into structured data to facilitate candidate search for recruiters.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
manualDesc: We assume that the manual has a hierarchical section structure, using the lowest section titles as basic unit for chunking documents.
Therefore, figures and tables in the same section will not be separated, which may result in larger chunk sizes.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
tableDesc: Supported file formats are XLSX and CSV/TXT.
Here are some prerequisites and tips:
For CSV or TXT file, the delimiter between columns must be TAB.
The first row must be column headers.

Column headers must be meaningful terms to aid your LLM's understanding. It is good practice to juxtapose synonyms separated by a slash '/' and to enumerate values using brackets, for example: 'Gender/Sex (male, female)'.
Here are some examples of headers:
supplier/vendor'TAB'Color (Yellow, Blue, Brown)'TAB'Sex/Gender (male, female)'TAB'size (M, L, XL, XXL)
Every row in table will be treated as a chunk.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
paperDesc: Papers will be split by section, such as abstract, 1.1, 1.2.

This approach enables the LLM to summarize the paper more effectively and to provide more comprehensive, understandable responses. However, it also increases the context for AI conversations and adds to the computational cost for the LLM.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
bookDesc: Supported file formats are DOCX, PDF, TXT.
For each book in PDF, please set the page ranges to remove unwanted information and reduce analysis time.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
lawsDesc: Supported file formats are DOCX, PDF, TXT.
Legal documents typically follow a rigorous writing format. We use text feature to identify split point.
The chunk has a granularity consistent with 'ARTICLE', ensuring all upper level text is included in the chunk.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
presentationDesc: Supported file formats are PDF, PPTX.
Every page in the slides is treated as a chunk, with its thumbnail image stored.
This chunk method is automatically applied to all uploaded PPT files, so you do not need to specify it manually.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
oneDesc: Supported file formats are DOCX, XLSX, XLS (Excel97~2003), PDF, TXT.
This method treats each document in its entirety as a chunk.
Applicable when you require the LLM to summarize the entire document, provided it can handle that amount of context length.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.
tagDesc: A knowledge base using the 'Tag' chunk method functions as a tag set. Other knowledge bases can use it to tag their own chunks, and queries to these knowledge bases will also be tagged using this tag set.
Knowledge base using 'Tag' as a chunk method will NOT be involved in a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) process.
Each chunk in this knowledge base is an independent description-tag pair.
Supported file formats include XLSX and CSV/TXT:

If a file is in XLSX format, it should contain two columns without headers: one for tag descriptions and the other for tag names, with the Description column preceding the Tag column. Multiple sheets are acceptable, provided the columns are properly structured.
If a file is in CSV/TXT format, it must be UTF-8 encoded with TAB as the delimiter to separate descriptions and tags.
In a Tag column, comma is used to separate tags.
Lines of texts that fail to follow the above rules will be ignored.
The following screenshots are provided for clarity.

setup: Go to the Google Cloud Console, create a service account, and enable the Google Drive API.
Go to Configuration Center
Generate and download the JSON key file.
In the target Google Drive folder, add the service account email as a collaborator with Read permission.
Log in to the AWS Management Console, create an IAM user, and grant it S3 read permissions.
Go to Configuration Center
Generate the access keys (Access Key ID & Secret Access Key).
Ensure that SMB sharing is enabled on the NAS server.
Recommend creating a dedicated read-only account for the system.
Obtain the server IP, shared folder name (optional), username, and password.
Go to the Notion Integrations page, create a new integration, and obtain the token.
Go to Configuration Center
Grant the integration at least Read content permission.
Share the integration with the target page or database.
Visit the Trello Developer page, create a Power-Up, and generate the API Key.
Go to Configuration Center
Manually generate the Token (authorization required).
Enable two-step verification on your Google account.
Go to Configuration Center
Generate an App Password (not your email login password).
Create a service account in the Google Cloud Console and enable the Google Cloud Storage API.
Go to Configuration Center
Generate and download the access keys (JSON or HMAC key).
